$comment: First-load JavaScript per route, in kilobytes: the decoded bytes a browser
downloads to render the route on a cold load of the standalone production
build, with Next's router prefetch for the links on the page not counted.
Uncompressed: what ships over the wire is smaller, but this is the number
that tracks what was added, and it does not move when compression
settings do.
Measured rather than read out of Next's build output. The size columns are
gone from `next build` in 16.x and the manifests underneath are
undocumented internals that move between versions; what the browser
downloads is what the budget is about, and it survives the bundler being
replaced.
Reset on 2026-09-13 from the prefetch-off measurement plus ~15%, rounded up
to 10 kB. The budgets before that date measured the wrong thing: they
counted every chunk loaded before the network went idle, which includes
what Next prefetches for a route's visible links. So a route's number was
its own code plus the screens it links to — 95 to 250 kB of every figure —
and it was not repeatable: /offers measured 871.5 and 885.2 kB from the
same build, depending on which links had prefetched in time. Two
prefetch-off runs of that build measured every route identically (G-112).
The 706.4 kB 'shared shell' the earlier comment described was partly the
change-set screen, prefetched from links present on every page.
/login is unchanged at 590: it renders before the shell and links nowhere,
so prefetch never touched its number.
The descriptor registry (40 kB) and the panel registry with the list-detail
host (54 kB) still load whole on every route that touches either — that is
most of what /offers, /creatives and /settings carry above the shell
(G-111). When W-080 splits them, measure with
scripts/measure-route-payload.mjs and lower these to match.
Raising a budget is a decision, not a formality: say in the commit message
what got bigger and why it earns its place.
